headline: Bank of Canada Holds at 2.25% as May Unemployment Sits at 6.6% and Housing Starts Reach 279,317 SAAR

facts.statement: Bank of Canada held overnight rate at 2.25% on June 10 — second consecutive hold, paired with the June Monetary Policy Report.
facts.source_title: Bank of Canada — Rate Decision press release, June 10, 2026
connections: 6,426 active Canadian projects ($1,536.5B aggregate) finance against the GoC yield curve
257 residential projects ($36.2B) face mortgage-renewal pricing anchored on the 5Y GoC yield, currently 3.04%
GoC 2s10s spread +64 bps; bull-flattening over the month and year

facts.statement: Real GDP contracted 0.1% m/m in March 2026 (released May 15); April flash estimate +0.4% per StatCan advance reading.
facts.source_title: StatCan Daily — Real GDP by industry, March 2026
connections: Manufacturing (31-33) sector m/m +0.4%, yy -2.5% — links to 346 active manufacturing projects ($70.0B)
Construction (23) m/m -0.6%, yy -1.5% — links to 1,497 infrastructure projects ($214.0B)

facts.statement: CPI snapshot reading +2.8% YoY (May reference); formal May print scheduled June 17 alongside FOMC SEP decision.
connections: Average hourly wage -1.4% m/m to $37.24 (May LFS) — composition shift toward lower-wage industries (accommodation/food +4.3% m/m headcount, retail -1.8%)
Household savings rate 3.5% Q1 (down 0.2 pp q/q from 3.7%)

facts.statement: Unemployment rate 6.6% in May (StatCan LFS June 6 release); participation rate 65.0%, employment rate 60.7%.
facts.source_title: StatCan Daily — Labour Force Survey, May 2026
connections: Agriculture employment +8.6% m/m to 240.1k; accommodation/food +4.3% m/m to 1,204.2k; retail -1.8% m/m to 2,237.5k; manufacturing -0.5% m/m to 243.2k; mining/oil-gas -0.5% m/m to 343.0k

facts.statement: Housing starts at 279,317 SAAR in May per CMHC (released June 15); April unadjusted total 21,805 units (+33.0% m/m).
facts.source_title: CMHC — Monthly Housing Starts Construction Data Tables
connections: Multi-unit starts +34.3% m/m vs March; singles +25.4% m/m. NHPI -0.4% m/m in April (first negative print after flat-to-rising months).
Residential permits -5.5% m/m to $7,482.9M; non-residential -10.5% m/m to $5,008.2M (StatCan 34-10-0292, April)

facts.statement: WTI crude fell 11.7% week-over-week to $80.58/bbl; Brent -11.7% w/w to $83.23/bbl — partial reversal of recent supply-shock premium.
connections: WTI is $80.58/bbl vs typical $74-76 breakeven cluster cited by the cross-reference engine for Alberta oil-sands records
Links to 89 active oil & gas projects ($63.2B) — sensitivity to WTI move is a database fact, not a directional call
April energy exports +9.7% m/m to $19.88B per StatCan 12-10-0163

indicatorContextLines.bocRate: The Bank of Canada held the overnight rate at 2.25% on June 10, the second consecutive hold, alongside the June Monetary Policy Report. The 5Y GoC benchmark is at 3.04%, the mortgage-renewal anchor.
indicatorContextLines.cpi: Headline CPI sits at +2.8% YoY (May reference snapshot, June 8 stamp). Formal May print scheduled for June 17 alongside the FOMC SEP decision. Core trim 2.0% and core median 2.0% remain within the BoC control band.
indicatorContextLines.unemployment: Unemployment rate at 6.6% in May (Labour Force Survey released June 6). Participation rate 65.0%, employment rate 60.7%. Average hourly wage fell 1.4% m/m to $37.24, reflecting composition shift toward lower-wage industries.
indicatorContextLines.housingStarts: CMHC May 2026 SAAR at 279,317. April unadjusted total 21,805 units (singles 3,063, multi 18,742). New housing price index 121.1 in April (-0.4% m/m).
indicatorContextLines.realGdp: March monthly real GDP at basic prices contracted 0.1% m/m. April flash estimate +0.4% per StatCan advance reading. Federal Q1 2026 GDP advance estimate referenced in BoC June MPR.

Housing affordability: New housing price index -0.4% m/m in April (first negative print after flat-to-rising months); 5Y GoC at 3.04% (-15 bps YoY) anchors mortgage renewals
Jobs and hours: services hiring tilted to accommodation/food +4.3% m/m; retail -1.8% m/m; mining/manufacturing flat-to-down
Savings: household savings rate 3.5% in Q1 2026, down 0.2 pp from 3.7% in Q4 2025
Federal fiscal: Spring Economic Update 2026 — $51B infrastructure commitments, new sovereign fund, CCUS-EOR expansion to Investment Tax Credit
Trade overhang: CUSMA review open; Trump administration 100% tariff threat referenced in prior-edition briefing
Energy prices: WTI down to $80.58/bbl from $105.42 a month ago (-23.6%) — gasoline-relevant pass-through pending
Savings yields: 2Y GoC 2.76% (-22 bps YoY) — GIC anchor
